description: Operator intent extrapolation — inferred, explicit, and implicit goals across UMH and Trinity apps, grounded in conversation and source truth evidence
operator_intent_summary: The operator wants UMH to extrapolate imperfect founder intent into a technically grounded end state. The operator wants Socratic questions for gaps. The operator wants to remain in the loop for questions, contradictions, clarifications, and decisions. Once operator and UMH are aligned on the docs/design boundary, UMH may operate more autonomously inside that boundary. Autonomy requires both approval and sufficient technical grounding.
inferred_goals: Build three separate, production-quality SaaS products (EOS, CreatorOS, LyfeOS) on a shared technology stack
Use UMH as the orchestration, governance, and intelligence layer across all products
Reach $10K/month net profit from Initiate Arena (EOS product) as the first revenue milestone
Maintain complete operator control over product scope, architecture, and deployment decisions
Move from pre-revenue to revenue-generating as fast as possible without sacrificing production quality
Use proven, managed services (Fly.io, Neon, Clerk) to minimize operational overhead
Keep each product independent while sharing standards and intelligence through UMH
explicit_goals: Every product end-state design must include the full 13-layer production stack
The operator must remain in the loop for questions, contradictions, clarifications, and decisions
No implementation until design is ratified
No app collapse — products remain separate
Feature build remains blocked until convergence decisions are ratified
Production truth promotion requires verified gates
implicit_goals: Quality over speed — the operator is willing to delay implementation to get the design right
Trust but verify — UMH can recommend but must not decide unilaterally
CompoundING system — each phase builds on the last, nothing is throwaway
Governance as a feature — the ability to govern and approve is itself valuable, not overhead
Documentation as insurance — design docs are not busywork, they prevent expensive mistakes
LyfeOS as the proof point — most mature product, validates the approach before applying to others

UMH.role: Orchestration, governance, production truth, cross-app intelligence
UMH.intent: UMH is the brain that coordinates everything. It does not own product UX but owns the decision-making, sequencing, risk gating, and source truth for all products.

EOS.role: Entrepreneur operating system — primary revenue vehicle (Initiate Arena)
EOS.intent: Get EOS to production-quality deployment as the first revenue-generating product. Beast branch is likely the canonical source (3x more complete) but needs validation. Clerk auth already integrated on Beast.
EOS.confidence: MEDIUM — source strategy (DEC-145-001) unresolved. Beast vs GitHub main is the key decision.
evidence: Initiate Arena is the revenue product

CreatorOS.role: Creator platform — content creation, community, courses
CreatorOS.intent: Fix the critical auth bypass first. Then define MVP scope. CreatorOS is secondary to EOS for revenue priority but needs its security vulnerability eliminated.
CreatorOS.confidence: MEDIUM — MVP scope (DEC-145-002) unresolved. Auth bypass is clearly P0.

LyfeOS.role: Life optimization platform — habits, goals, AI coaching
LyfeOS.intent: LyfeOS is the most mature and already deployed. Strengthen what exists: production harden, add observability, verify backups, then plan UMH connection and Clerk migration.
LyfeOS.confidence: HIGH — clearest path of the three products.

shared_trinity_intent: Build on a shared technology stack (React/Vite/TypeScript/Express/Drizzle/Neon/Clerk/Fly.io) with shared standards (OS Platform Standard v2) but maintain separate product identities, separate databases, separate deployments, and separate user experiences.

device_role_intent.vps: UMH orchestrator, control plane, governance — lightweight, always-on
device_role_intent.beast: App development workhorse, heavy compute, model inference — not always-on
device_role_intent.fly_io: Production hosting for cockpit and Trinity apps
device_role_intent.mobile: Operator approval surface, remote control — not a development device

autonomy_intent: Graduated autonomy. UMH can work autonomously ONLY inside an approved execution boundary. Outside the boundary, UMH must ask. Approved boundaries require: ratified design doc, approved convergence plan, approved work packet, clear acceptance criteria, clear blocked actions, clear validation plan.
governance_intent: Socratic governance. UMH surfaces questions, contradictions, and clarifications. Operator decides. System recommends but does not choose. Operator decisions are tracked, versioned, and enforced.
production_stack_intent: Every product must define its complete 13-layer production stack before feature build begins. This is not optional DevOps — it is required product design. Infrastructure gaps block deployment. Security gaps block deployment. Observability gaps block deployment.
unresolved_intent_gaps: CreatorOS: What is the MVP scope? (DEC-145-002)
Shared: Clerk migration order across apps? (DEC-145-004)
Shared: When does feature build unlock?
Shared: When does infrastructure implementation unlock?
UMH: What level of cross-app integration is desired in the near term?
All: What does 'production ready' mean for each product? (minimum viable production)
system_recommendations: Promote Beast branch for EOS (DEC-145-001 option A) after build validation and secret scan
Start with Creator+Course MVP scope for CreatorOS (DEC-145-002 option B) after auth fix
Canonize LyfeOS PRD v2.0 (DEC-145-003 option C) as it reflects actual deployed state
Fix CreatorOS auth bypass FIRST regardless of other sequencing decisions
Verify LyfeOS backups immediately — it is deployed with user data and no confirmed recovery
Define 'minimum viable production' per product so readiness gates have concrete criteria
operator_decisions_needed: DEC-145-005: OS Platform Standard v2 scope
NEW: Minimum viable production definition per app
